<reason>B won the central comparison between checking readiness before expansion and enforcing conduct afterward. A raised meaningful concerns about unnecessary requirements and municipal delays, but B answered with proportionate commitments, existing-service options, and an honest defense of withholding extensions when essential arrangements are absent. A repeatedly reduced enforceable preparation to paperwork and overstated agency silence as an automatic veto. Its alternative never adequately answered the risk of preventable failures before inspections catch up.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B decisively answered A’s claim that a cleanup rota proves nothing: confirming someone is assigned and available can reduce failure without guaranteeing compliance. This exposed A’s unsupported leap from imperfect advance verification to identical risk under both systems.</best_rebuttal>
